rows.author: C130
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PHILIPPINE COCONUT AUTHORITY BY WAY OF INCREASED SMALL COCONUT FARMERS AND FARM WORKERS' PARTICIPATION IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE COCONUT INDUSTRY
rows.abstract: "Coconut Industry Development Act of 2001". This proposed measures substantiates the State policy to: (1) ADOPT THE NECESSARY MEASURES THAT WILL ARREST THE SERIOUS PROBLEMS THAT BESET THE COCONUT INDUSTRY, THREATENING ITS VIABILITY; (2) PROMOTE THERAPID INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT AND GROWTH OF THE COCONUT AND OTHER PAL OIL INDUSTRY IN ALL ITS ASPECTS AND TO ENSURE THAT THE COCONUT FARMERS, SPECIALLY THE SMALL COCONUT FARMERS, TILLERS, WORKERS AND OWNER-CULTIVATO RS WHO COMPRISE THE OVERWHELMING MAJORITY OF THE PEOPLE IN THE COCONUT INDUSTRY, BECOME DIRECT PARTICIPANTS IN, AND BENEFICIARIES OF, SUCH DEVELOPMENT AND GROWTH; AND (3) TO PROMOTE AND INSTITUTIONALIZ E THE PARTICIPATION OF NON-GOVERNMENT ORGANIZATIONS AND PEOPLE'S ORGANIZATION IN THHE COCONUT INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENT PROCESS.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-12-10

rows.author: D015
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-12-17, transmitted to on 2003-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2004-01-06
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A CORPORATE BODY TO BE KNOWN AS THE `THE IFUGAO TERRACES AUTHORITY' UNDER THE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE PHILIPPINES, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES AS WELL AS APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Substituted by HB06475

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO DEFINE AND GUARANTEE PUBLIC SECTOR UNIONISM IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Public Sector Unionism Act of 2001". Under this proposed measure and consistent with the aforesaid constitutional provision, a duly recognized union of government employees is ensured of the right to act as official body representative of its members for purposes of collective bargaining and negotiations. This bill further put in place a mechanism that ensures the recognition of the right of government workers/employe es for a peaceful assembly and their right to petition government to rause and ease their grievances. > This bill, likewise, seeks to create a PUBLIC SECTOR LABOR RELATIONS BOARD which shall gurantee government employees the right to self-organizati on and collective bargaining.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-12-10

rows.author: B035
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL IN BARANGAY LIONG, MUNICIPALITY OF CATAINGAN, PROVINCE OF MASBATE, TO BE KNOWN AS `LIONG NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL,' AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-12-10

rows.author: D087
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING BANKS FROM IMPOSING FEES OR CHARGES ON SAVINGS OR CURRENT ACCOUNTS FALLING BELOW THE REQUIRED MINIMUM MAINTAINING BALANCE AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: It shall be unlawful for any bank, whether government-owne d or private, local or foreign to impose fees or charges on depositors who cannot comply with the required minimum maintaining balance in savings or current accounts by deducting certain amounts from depositor's remaining balance of his/her deposit.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2001-12-10

rows.author: D087
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ADDITIONAL PRIVILEGES AND INCENTIVES TO DISABLED PERSONS SIMILAR TO THOSE ENJOYED BY SENIOR CITIZENS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7277, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MAGNA CARTA FOR DISABLED PERSONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Over the years we see many persons with disability that try to make a living despite of their physical handicap. Others are lazy and do not seel to care about their future and just rely on their parents or relatives for their living. It is but fitting that the state should give persons with disability additional privilege and incentives similar to those enjoyed by senior citizens. > This bill seeks to grant 20% discount from all establishments, 10% discount in the purchase of medicines, exemption from the payment of individual income taxes, and full medical and dental services in government establishments, among others.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2001-12-10

rows.author: D087
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL GAMBLING IMPACT STUDY AND POLICY COMMISSION TO REVIEW, STUDY AND ASSESS THE IMPACT OF GAMBLING AND OTHER SIMILAR FORMS OF GAMES AND AMUSEMENTS AND RECOMMEND POLICY, INSTITUTIONAL AND SIMILAR MEASURES, APPROPRIATING FUNDSTHEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Gambling, as many people would say brings more harm than good. As a matter of fact many families have been broken due to gambling. On the other hand, it also helps build roads and bridges, schools, water system, and other forms of infrastructure projects from its proceeds. Its many advantages and disadvantages are still up for debate until this time because nobody knows exactly in factual terms if gambling indeed brings more harm than good. > It is in this context that this bill is filed to determine the social and economic impact of gambling in the country. It seeks the establishment of the "National Gambling Impact Study and Policy Commission." The Commission shall conduct a comprehensive, legal, scientific and factual study oof the social and economic impacts of gambling in the Philippines.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-12-10

rows.author: D087
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ADDITIONAL EXEMPTION OF TWENTY THOUSAND PESOS (P20,000.00) FOR MARRIED INDIVIDUALS WHOSE SPOUSE IS A NONWORKING SPOUSE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 35(A) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: Rationale: Many non-working spouses are college graduates and some have college units but opted not to work and decided to stay home to take of the childre. These people value their family very much instead of working to earn more money. Just as theState recognizes the Filipino family as the foundation of the nation, it is but fitting to provide these citizens (the non-working spouses who take care of the family) a tax relief by granting them additional individual tax exemption of P20,000.00.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-12-10

rows.author: D087
rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE HIRING OF CASUAL EMPLOYEES IN THE GOVERNMENT, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to provide security of tenure to thousands of government employees who hold casual appointments in the service. They shall not be terminated anytime before the expiration of the contract or within the period for which they are hiredexcept for unsatisfactory conduct or want or capacity. > Casual employees who had served satisfactorily for a continuous period of five years in a particular position shall be automatically included in the plantilla of regular positions.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-12-10

rows.author: D001
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE COCONUT LEVY FUNDS AS PUBLIC FUNDS, CREATING THE COCONUT INDUSTRY REHABILITATION AND DEVELOPMENT FUND AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The coconut levy funds  or the enforced contributions levied by the State on the coconut farmers pursuant to Repbulic Act No. 6260, Presidential Decree Nos. 276, 582, 1841 and other pertinent amendatory laws, including all income, interests, proceeds or profits derived therefrom, as well as all assets, properties and shares of stock procured or obtained with the use of such funds, which are under sequestration by the government, are hereby declared as public funds.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-12-10

rows.author: C016
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8560, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PHILIPPINE GEODETIC ENGINEERING ACT OF 1998, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill proposed AMENDMENTS to certain provisions of RA No. 8560, the Philippine Geodetic Engineering Act of 1998, such as: (1) The submission of survey plows of subdivided, consolidated and/or consolidated subdivision titled properties to the concerned government agencies FOR NUMBERING AND PROJECTION ON GOVERNMENT BASE MAPS AND FOR RECORDS PURPOSES ONLY; (2) ALLOWING registered JUNIOR GEODETIC ENGINEERS to register as geodetic engineers WITHOUT completing the Bachelor's Degree in Geodetic Engineering, subject to certain conditions; and (3) REPEAL of Section 24, and instead allow certain corporations to engage in CONSULTING SERVICE.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04738

rows.author: C117
rows.title_full: AN ACT RECOGNIZING DUAL CITIZENSHIP OF FOREIGN NATIONALS WHO WERE FILIPINOS OR WHO WERE OF FILIPINO ANCESTRY, UNDER CERTAIN CONDITIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8171, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: SECTION 1. Section 1 of Republic Act No. 8171 entitled, "An Act Providing for the Repatriation of Filipino Women Who Have Lost Their Philippine Citizenship by Marriage to Aliens and of Natural-Born Filipinos." is hereby amended to read as follows: "Section 1. NATURAL-BORN FILIPINOS WHO HAVE LOST THEIR PHILIPPINE CITIZENSHIP, INCLUDING THEIR MINOR CHILDREN, ON ACCOUNT OF POLITICAL OR ECONOMIC NECESSITY, OR WHO ACQUIRED FOREIGN CITIZENSHIP UNDER THE PRINCIPLE OF JUS SOLI OR BY REASON OF BIRTH ANDFilipino women who have lost their Philippine citizenship by marriage to aliens [natural-born Filipinos who have lost Philippine citizenship, including their minor children, on account of political or economic necessity] may reacquire Philippine cittizenship through repatriation WITHOUT RENOUNCING THEIR FOREIGN CITIZENSHIP[in the manner provided, in Section 4 of Commonwealth Act No. 65, as amended]; Provided, That the applicant is not a: x x x
rows.status: Substituted by HB04720

rows.author: C062
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR EFFECTIVE TRAINING AND PROGRAMS FOR WIDOWS, SINGLE PARENTS AND INDIVIDUALS ENTERING NONTRADITIONAL EMPLOYMENT
rows.abstract: "Widows Employment Assistance and Lifeskills Act of 2001". Rationale: WIDOWS and SINGLE PARENTS represent an untapped resource to enter unfilled and available positions in information technology sector, their education and training needs not being given considerable attention and assistance by the government, for lack of necessary programs and laws that could redound to their benefits and help them become more independent, self-reliant and productive citizens of the Republic. > This bill aims to fill in there needs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-12-10

rows.author: C062
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STRENGTHEN AND EFFECTUATE EQUALITY OF OPPORTUNITY FOR ALL FILIPINO WOMEN, ESTABLISHING AND IMPLEMENTING MACHINERY THEREFOR, APPROPRIATING FUNDS IN SUPPORT THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Equality of Opportunity for All Filipino Women Act of 2001". It is hereby declared UNLAWFUL, and contrary to public policy, on the part of any party to any service relationship, to engage in the practice of inequality against women in such relationship, or commit any act of discriminating against any women in such relationship, based primarily on sex. > "SERVICE RELATIONSHIP" shall include employment of any kind, the hiring of professionals or the contracting of any piece of work, by which services are performed for a compensation in any form or any kind, under the control of the hirer or his representative, with respect to the result only, or with respect to the details and manner of performance as well as the result thereof.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN since 2001-12-10

rows.author: D032
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING RETIREMENT BENEFITS TO ALL ELECTED AND APPOINTED BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Every punong barangay, sangguniang barangay member, chairman of the kabataan barangay, barangay secretary, barangay treasurer and members of barangay tanod brigades shall be provided with retirement benefits under a retirement plan to be administered and managed by the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS). > A barangay official, who has reached the age of sixty-five (65) years old and has at least twenty (20) years of government service, shall be retired. Upon retirement, he shall be entitled to receive retirement benefits.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-12-10

rows.author: D032
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO EXCLUDE THE PRINT AND BROADCAST MEDIA ESTABLISHMENTS FROM SEEKING EXEMPTION FROM THE WAGE ORDER ISSUED PURSUANT TO REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6727, AS AMENDED AND ITS IMPLEMENTING RULES AND REGULATION AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: The press or media, in a democracy, practically constitutes the fourth branch of government. They key position it occupies in ferreting out factsm in molding public opinion, in channeling the actions of the Executive and the Legislature,and all agencies of the government along lines conducive to public welfare vests it with tremendous power and influence. However, some members of the press are forced to take advantage of their influence, considering the vital role played by the media in our society, by resorting to unethical forms of fund raising brought about by lack of financial security in the practice of their vocation. Yet, this occurrence may have been prevented should all or small media and press compatriots have enjoyedd rightful compensation for their services to the public. > There is an urgent need therefor for the enactment of this measure so as not to leave any loopholes in the implementation of the existing minimum wage law.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-12-10

rows.author: D006
rows.title_full: AN ACT SEPARATING THE VETERANS MEMORIAL MEDICAL CENTER FROM THE PHILIPPINE VETERANS AFFAIRS OFFICE, AND ELEVATING IT INTO A BUREAU UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENSE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE LETTER OF INSTRUCTION NUMBER NINETEEN
rows.abstract: Rationale: There is an urgent need to elevate the Veterans Memorial Medical Center (VMMC) to a bureau level to attain its four-fold mission and objectives more effectively and efficiently, to wit: (1) Patient Care; (2) Medical Education and Training; (3) Research; and (4) Civic Action Programs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-12-10

rows.author: D019
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE DANGEROUS DRUGS ACT OF 2001 REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6425, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to AMEND the provisions of the Dangerous Drugs Act of 1972 to make it more effective in addressing the drug problem in our society the extent of which, at present, has already assumed very severe and alarming proportions. > To curb the incessant surge in the crime rate brought about by drug-related incidents, authorities need stronger measures to combat the drug menace in the form of a law that encompasses a wider scope and provides stiffer penalties for offenders.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04433

rows.title_full: AN ACT CHANGING THE MANNER BY WHICH THE POSITIONS OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN OFFICIALS ARE FILLED, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PERTINENT PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, ANDBATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: All BARANGAY and SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN OFFICIALS will be APPOINTED, rather than elected, by a Municipal - Barangay Monitoring Council/City - Barangay Monitoring Council composed of members coming from (1) Religious Organizations; (2) Farmer Cooperatives; (3) Students Organizations; (4) Business Organizations; (5) Senior Citizens Organization; (6) Women's Organizations; and (7) Cultural Organizations, who shall elect one (1) from among their respective sectors a representative to form the council.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-12-10

rows.abstract: "Muslim Affairs and Development Act of 2001". All Muslim Filipinos who have communities in the regional or national level shall be the subject of development programs by the government as provided for in this Act.

rows.author: C101
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8291 AND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8292, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES(RE: GSIS & SSS HOUSING LOANS)
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend certain provisions of Republic Acts 8291 and 8292, otherwise known as the GSIS Law of 1997 and the Social Security Law of 1997, respectively, in order to provide for a preferential mode or scheme of granting housing loans tomembers of the GSIS and the SSS at affordable rates of interest and in accordance with, and giving due consideration to, their ability to pay. > This bill principally states that HOUSING LOANS GRANTED TO MEMBERS SHALL BE AT PREFERENTIAL RATES OF INTEREST NOT EXCEEDING ONE HALF (1/2) OF THE PREVAILING RATE AND UNDER SUCH PAYMENT SCHEMES AND OTHER TERMS AND CONDITIONS AS ARE REFLECTIVE OF OR IN CONSONANCE WITH THEIR ABILITY TO PAY AND PROMOTIVE OF THEIR BASIC ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL RIGHT TO DECENT HHOUSING.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-12-11

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE DISPOSITION OF SMUGGLED AGRICULTURAL GOODS, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF TARIFF AND CUSTOMS CODE, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This bill adds the following provision regarding PROPERTY SUBJECT TO SALE under Section 2601 of the Tariff and Customs Code: ANY AGRICULTURAL PRODUCT COVERED BY SCHEDULES I AND II OF THIS CODE SUBJECT TO FORFEITURE IN FAVOR OF THE GOVERNMENT, PROVIDED THAT IN ALL SUCH CASES INVOLVING SAID AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS, THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT AGENCY CONCERNED THROUGH THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FOOD OR ANY OF ITS ATTACHED AGENCIES SHALL BE GIVEN THE AUTHORITY TO DISPOSE OF THE SAME THROUGH LOCALDISPOSITION OR RE-EXPORTATION, WHICHEVER SHALL BE TO THE BEST INTEREST OF THE GENERAL PUBLIC AND THE LOCAL PRODUCERS. THE BUREAU OF CUSTOMS SHALL TRANSFER CUSTODY OF THE SAME TO THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT AGENCY CONCERNED WITHIN FIFTEEN DAYS FROM THE TIIME THE FORFEITURE HAS BECOME FINAL AND EXECUTORY.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-12-11

rows.author: C075
rows.title_full: AN ACT ENTITLED REVISED PUBLIC LAND ACT OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: With the advent of modern technologies and in the light of the present needs of times, this Public Land Act can be considered obsolete and unrealistic. This bill seeks to UPDATE and SUPPLEMENT existing legal provisions on the management and disposition of public lands in order to consolidate therein related provisions of certain Presidential Decrees, Batas Pambansa and other existing laws. With the passage of the legislative measures, the nagging problems affecting public land, suchas the proliferation of fake titles, sustainable use of foreshore lands and problems related with land survey matters, can be aptly addressed through responsive regulatory mechanism.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2001-12-11

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING POSITIONS IN THE STAFFING PATTERN AND PLANTILLA OF THE BUREAU OF INTERNAL REVENUE AND THE BUREAU OF CUSTOMS AS POLICY-DETERMIN ING, PRIMARILY CONFIDENTIAL AND HIGHLY TECHNICAL, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "BIR Personnel Reform Act of 2001". All positions in the staffinf pattern and plantilla of the bureau of Internal Revenue directly and expressly tasked with the enforcement and implementation of tax laws or directly involved or connected with the assessment and collection of taxes are hereby declared as policy-determin ing, primarily confidential and highly technical. > any personnel who may displaced or separeated as a consuquence of the implementation of this Act or who may choose to discontinue his services shall be entitled to such retirement benefits, if qualified, provided under existing laws, rules and regulations. Otherwise, he shall be paid separation benefits equivalent to one and one-half months salary for every year of servicein the government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-12-12

rows.author: B020
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM DOCUMENTARY STAMP TAX THE BORROWING AND LENDING OF SECURITIES UNDER THE AUSPICES OF THE LOCAL STOCK EXCHANGE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 180 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: THE BORROWING AND LENDING OF SECURITIES EXECUTED UNDER THE SECURITIES BORROWING AND LENDING PROGRAM OF THE LOCAL STOCK EXCHANGE FOR PURPOSES OF TRADING STRATEGIES OF EITHER THE BORROWER OR LENDER, SHALL BE EXEMPT FROM THE PAYMENT OF THE DOCUMENTARYSTAMP TAX IMPOSED HEREON. FOR PURPOSES OF THIS SECTION, THE BORROWING AND LENDING OF SECURITIES SHALL MEAN THE TRANSFER OF SECURITIES FROM AN INVESTOR'S PORTFOLIO TO A BORROWER OR LENDER WITHOUT A CHANGE IN BENEFICIAL OWNERSHIP OF THE BORROWED SECURITIES AND EXECUTED TO SUPPORT TRADING STRATEGIES OF THE BORROWER OR THE LENDER.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTIES FOR ELECTION OFFENSES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE XXII, SECTIONS 264 AND 265 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BILANG 881, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Since the objective of election is to choose who are truly the representatives of the pople, various measures have been taken to safeguard the conduct of election. One such measure is provided in Section 27 (b) of the "Electoral Reform Law of 1987" which makes it an election offense for any member of the board of inspectors or board of canvassers to tamper with, increase or decrease the vote received by a candidate or to refuse, after proper verification and hearing, to credit votesor deduct such tampered votes. The penalties provided for the offense, as provided Section 264 of the Omnibus Election Code is one to sux years of imprisonment, without probation. However, the measure has not deterred the commission of this offense.It even appears that there is an increasing use of this fraudulent method to win election."Opera tion dagdag-bawas", which figuratively describes the method, was perceived to have been used during the 1992, 1995, 1998, and 2001 elections. > This bill

rows.abstract: Filipino athletes, who have brought honor and prestige to the Philippines by being world champions or gold medallists in internationally -acclaimed professional or amateur competitions, shall,upon reaching the age of sixty years, be entitled to retirement benefit in the amount of TEN THOUSAND PESOS (P10,000.00) per month.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION OF ENDANGERED AND THREATENED SPECIES OF FISH, WILDLIFE AND PLANTS OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to protect and conserve the endangered species of fish, wildlife and plants of the Philippines. Forest denudation is one major reason for the imbalance in the ecosystem. The problem of forest destruction is very much related to wildlife protection because most of the wildlife use the forest for their habitat. Without the forests, there will likewise be no food source for them.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2001-12-18

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MODERNIZATION OF THE SCHOOL HEALTH AND NUTRITION PROGRAM (SHNP) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION, CULTURE AND SPORTS, AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The proposed SCHOOL HEALTH AND NUTRITION PROGRAM (SHNP) shall have the following thrusts: (1) The development of an efficient and effective health care delivery sysatem among schools; (2) The development, evaluation and application of appropriate methods and procedures in preventive health care; (3) The development of reforms in the management of human and material resources; and (4) The acquisition and upgrading of appropriate equipment and technology.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-12-18

rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING PROSTITUTION, DEFINING THE PERSONS LIABLE THEREFOR, PROVIDING MEASURES AND SUPPORT SERVICES FOR ITS VICTIMS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This proposed measure is premised on the following policies of the State: > The State --- (1) recognizes prostitution as a human rights violation which calls for coordinate and sustained response from all agencies of government; (2) recognizes that women and children are systematically victimized by and in the system of prostitution and must, therefore, be given protection and support by the State, instead of being treated as criminals; and (3) recognizes international commitments onthe eradication of sexual exploitation in all forms of gender-based violence.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-12-18

rows.abstract: "Anti-Organized Crime Act of 2001". This amendment is aimed at unburdening the administrative laod both of the Insurance Commission and the insurers by extending the term of license so that agents can concentrate more on the business of selling insurance products and, consequently, further spur the growth of the insurance industry.

Portia Sorority, Department of Women and Development Studies of the U.P. College of Social Work and Community Development, COURAGE and GABRIELA maintain that as a matter of right, unmarried pregnant women in government service should also enjoy maternity leave benefits as unmarried pregnant women in the private sector do. rows.abstract: "Anti-Cyber Crime Law". It is the policy of the State to protect the society against the upsurge of computer fraud, destruction of electronic systems and properties and proliferation of crimes brought about by the continuing globalization of computer networks. It is imperative for us to maintain the confidentiality , integrity, reliability and availability of computer systems, networks and computer data in the furtherance of our national interest and security. The individual efforts of the concerned agencies should harmoniously complement one another.

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES OFFICERS TRAINING PROGRAM, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: A training program for future officers in the Armed Forces of the Philippines shall be established for each of the major branches: The Army, Air Force and the Navy. Five students for every branch shall be admitted into the program every year, sent into a reputable university at the choice of the General Headquarters to complete any relevant four-year course.  Full scholarship shall be granted to the qualified candidates covering tuition fees, board and lodging, meals, transportation, clothing and laundry plus a monthly allowance equivalent to the salary of a duty sergeant, all to be provided by the administering branch.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2001-12-19

rows.author: A071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR PUBLIC LIABILITY INSURANCE FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROVIDING IMMEDIATE RELIEF TO PERSONS AFFECTED BY ACCIDENT ARISING FROM THE OPERATIONS OR INCIDENTAL TO THE OPERATIONS OF ESTABLISHMENTS, ENTERPRISES, PUBLIC UTILITIES AND VEHICLES,BUILDINGS, MACHINERY AND THEIR ACCESSORIES
rows.abstract: "Public Liability Insurance Act of 2001". Rationale: The main point of contention in major disasters and tragedies is the issue on public liability: who are primarily liable for damages for the loss of lives and destruction of properties? Concernedentities often pass the blame to others. the most common defense used to escape liability is to declare them as accidents or call the disasters as the "acts of God" or force majeure. This defense usually deflects the responsibility and liability fromthe owners or operators and their agents and servants. > To address this concern, this public utility law must be enacted to hold owners and operators directly and primarily responsible for injuries and damages arising from the operation or incidenttal to the operation of their enterprise, establishments, property, personnel and their accessories.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2001-12-19

rows.abstract: Illegitimate children shall use the surname and shall be under the parental authority of their mother, and shall be entitled to support in conformity with this Code.
